title: Defaults for the Common Case
content:
What problem does this solve?
Sometimes one function input usually has the same value. A default places that common value in the function definition so callers may omit it. Callers can still replace the default for a particular call.

Use the default
  def greet(name, punctuation="!"):
      return f"Hello, {name}{punctuation}"
  greet("Ada")
Because the second argument is omitted, punctuation receives !.

Override it
  greet("Ada", "?")
A supplied positional argument replaces the default for that call.

Override by name
  greet(name="Ada", punctuation=".")
A keyword argument explicitly names the parameter it should replace. Required parameters must come before parameters that have defaults in the function definition.

Vocabulary after the behavior
A default parameter supplies a value when its argument is omitted. A keyword argument names the parameter at the call site. An override replaces the default for one call.
concepts: A default supplies a common value when an argument is omitted
A caller can override a default positionally or by keyword
Keyword arguments match values to parameter names
Required parameters come before defaulted parameters in a function definition

examples.title: Use the default
examples.explanation: No punctuation argument is supplied, so the default ! is used.

examples.title: Override it
examples.explanation: The second positional argument replaces the default for this call.

examples.title: Override by name
examples.explanation: source is overridden by name while tone keeps its default.

common_mistakes: Putting a required parameter after a defaulted parameter
Writing a body-level fallback instead of a signature default when the signature is the learning objective
Assuming a default cannot be overridden
Using a keyword that does not match any parameter name
Using mutable list/dict defaults before understanding shared references

exercises.title: Use the default
hints: The call provides only the required place argument.
Because status is omitted, Python uses the value written after = in the signature.
status becomes Review, so the output is Gate: Review.

exercises.title: Override positionally
hints: A second argument was supplied in this call.
That positional value matches the status parameter and replaces its default.
The output is Gate: Ready.

exercises.title: Override by name
hints: Only source is overridden by name.
tone is omitted, so it keeps soft; text receives clear.
The returned string is soft|tower|clear.

exercises.title: Which signature is valid?
exercises.prompt: Which function definition correctly makes message required while level defaults to `"NOTICE"`?
hints: Required parameters must appear before parameters with defaults.
Parameter names belong in the signature; literal argument values do not replace parameter names.
Choose `def log(message, level="NOTICE"):`.

exercises.title: One item by default
exercises.prompt: Complete the function signature so `format_supply("rope")` returns `1 x rope`, while callers may still pass another quantity.
hints: The default belongs in the function signature, not inside the body.
Give quantity the common value 1 with `=`.
Use `def format_supply(item, quantity=1):`.

exercises.title: Required before optional
exercises.prompt: This definition is invalid because a required parameter appears after a defaulted one. Repair only the parameter order so `destination` is required and `status` defaults to `"Review"`.
hints: The problem is in the order of the parameters, not the function body.
Put the required parameter first and the defaulted parameter second.
Use `def mark_dispatch(destination, status="Review"):`.

exercises.title: Default status helper
exercises.prompt: Write `format_status(name, status="Review")` from scratch. Return `<name>: <status>`. Calling it with only name must use Review; calling it with `status="Cleared"` must override the default.
hints: Keep the default in the signature and build one returned string from both parameter names.
Use an f-string and return it; do not print inside the function.
Return `f"{name}: {status}"`.
exercises.success_message: The helper uses its default when omitted and accepts both positional and keyword overrides.

exercises.title: Dispatch Log Builder
exercises.prompt: Write `log_entry(message, level="NOTICE", source="field")` so it returns `[<level>][<source>] <message>`. Then build exactly three strings in a `dispatch_log` list: `log_entry("gate checked")`, `log_entry("venom found", "ALERT")`, and `log_entry("signal clear", source="tower")`. Loop over the list and print each finished line.
hints: First make log_entry correct on its own: it should always return one formatted string using both defaults when they are omitted.
Build the list by calling the function three different ways: defaults, positional level override, keyword source override.
Finally loop over dispatch_log and print each returned string. Do not duplicate the formatting outside the function.

tests.expected:
[NOTICE][field] gate checked
[ALERT][field] venom found
[NOTICE][tower] signal clear

exercises.success_message: Dispatch log complete. One function handled the common case and two kinds of override, then older list/loop skills assembled the finished report.
